title: Pastry: crisp shortcrust, flaky rough puff and hollow choux

say: Pastry: crisp shortcrust, flaky rough puff, and hollow choux.
This is the video for module three of Advanced Baking and Pastry.
Pastry rewards precise temperature control. Shortcrust snaps because cold fat shortens the gluten.

say: You know shortcrust from meat pie. The ratio is 2 parts flour to 1 part cold butter, with a pinch of salt.

panel.heading: A crisp tart case, step by step
items: 2 parts flour to 1 part cold fat
Rub in to fine crumbs; water until it holds
Chill 30 minutes, roll to 3 mm
Ease into the tin, never stretch
Blind bake, then seal with egg

say: Rub the butter in quickly with cool fingertips until it looks like fine breadcrumbs. Add cold water a little at a time, and stop as soon as a handful holds together.

say: Wrap and chill at least 30 minutes to relax the gluten, then roll to about 3 millimetres.

say: Ease the pastry down into the corners. Stretched pastry pulls back and shrinks in the oven.

say: Blind bake the empty case with paper and baking beans, at about 190 to 200 degrees for roughly 15 minutes. Remove the beans, bake 5 to 10 minutes more, then brush with egg and bake 2 minutes to seal it under wet fillings.

panel.rule: Dough too soft? Chill it 10 minutes. Do not add flour.

say: Use equal weights of flour and cold butter. Toss the butter cubes in the flour, but do not rub them in. You want whole lumps.

panel.heading: Lamination with letter folds
items: Toss whole butter cubes in flour

Roll a long rectangle, fold in three
Quarter turn, repeat; chill when soft
Four folds in all, then bake hot

say: Add ice-cold water to make a rough dough with visible butter, then chill 20 minutes.

say: Turn it a quarter turn and repeat. If the butter looks soft or shiny, chill it. Melted butter gives tough, greasy pastry.

say: Each fold triples the layers: 3, then 9, 27, and 81 after four folds. Cut with a sharp knife, and bake at about 200 to 220 degrees so steam forms fast.

say: Bring the water, milk and butter to a full boil. Off the heat, tip in all the flour and beat hard until smooth.

panel.heading: Cook, beat, then the V test
items: Boil water, milk and butter; add flour
Stir on the heat until a film forms
Cool until just warm
Add egg gradually, to the V test
Bake hot; never open the door early

say: Stir on medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the pan bottom. This dries the paste.

say: Beat it in a bowl until just warm.

panel.heading: Cook, beat, then the V test

say: Add egg a little at a time. Eggs vary, so never add a fixed amount. Stop when the paste falls slowly from the spatula and leaves a V-shaped flag. Too much egg, and the shells spread flat.

panel.heading: Cook, beat, then the V test

Bake hot; never open the door early

say: Bake at about 200 degrees for 15 minutes, then about 180 for 15 to 20 more, without opening the door. Pierce each shell and dry it in the switched-off oven.

say: Egg and milk custards are ideal places for bacteria to grow. Pastry cream must bubble for a full 1 to 2 minutes. Cool it quickly in a shallow dish, keep it in the fridge, and use it within about 2 days.

Fill close to serving and keep chilled. Never leave in a warm room or hot car.
Cook until piping hot, not pink. Keep raw meat, boards and knives separate.

say: Fill choux as close to serving as possible, and keep filled pastries chilled.

say: Cook meat fillings until the centre is piping hot and no longer pink. Keep raw meat and its boards and knives away from finished food. And anything with a food safety doubt must be thrown away, never sold.

say: Write down weights, room temperature, chilling, oven setting, shelf and time for every batch. Change only one thing at a time when you test a fix.

panel.rule: Keep a batch record. Change one thing at a time.

say: To remember. Keep shortcrust cold and ease it into the tin. Give rough puff four letter folds and keep the butter cold. Dry the choux paste and use the V test.
Chill custard fillings fast. And find faults in order: ratio, temperature, handling, then baking.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Shortcrust: 2 to 1, cold, ease into tin
Rough puff: four letter folds, keep cold
Choux: dry the paste, use the V test
Chill custard fillings fast; keep cold
Ratio, temperature, handling, baking
